ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a three-dimensional drawing similar to a cube; each vertex angle of the original cube has been cut off; it can be seen that triangular cross-sections have formed at some corners, the original edges have become shorter line segments, and the dashed lines represent the obscured original cube structure. Then reason: The cube originally had 12 edges. After all 8 vertices are cut off, the middle of each original edge is still retained as a shorter edge, so 12 short edges are retained. Each cut-off vertex will produce a triangular cross-section, and this triangular cross-section has 3 new edges; there are 8 vertices in total, so the number of new edges is 8 × 3 = 24. The total number of edges is 12 + 24 = 36.

method.method_draft: Use the image to recognize the solid as a cube with every one of its 8 vertices truncated: the drawing shows triangular cut faces at corners and shortened remnants of the cube’s original edges. From the text, use the condition that all corners of the cube are cut off. Count edges by classification: the cube’s 12 original edges remain as shorter edges, and each of the 8 cut-off corners creates a triangular face contributing 3 new boundary edges. These new triangle edges are distinct from the shortened original edges, so the total is 12 + 8×3 = 36.
